You will create a private draft, choose an outline, preview its design, and publish a page readers can navigate.

## Before you start

Sign in to a Margin workspace where you can create and publish content. Have a specific reader and a small task in mind. For this walkthrough, our task is helping a teammate publish their first guide.

**You'll finish with:** one published guide, an automatically generated table of contents, and a shareable link.

## Choose the right starting point

Open **New → Guide**, then **Browse templates**.

[Tabs title="Choose your outline" variant="boxed"]
[Tab title="User guide"]
Choose **User guide** when readers need help understanding a product. The outline starts with an overview, getting started, everyday tasks, and troubleshooting.
[/Tab]
[Tab title="Playbook"]
Choose **Playbook** when readers need a repeatable process. The outline covers the trigger, prerequisites, steps, decisions, and completion checks.
[/Tab]
[/Tabs]

Select **Use this outline**. The prompts become ordinary Markdown that you can replace, rearrange, or remove.

## Write one useful task

Replace the title with a specific outcome, such as “Publish your first guide.” Explain the starting conditions before listing the actions.

### Make each step verifiable

A useful step has an action and a visible result:

> Open **New → Guide**. A new draft opens with the Guide label.

Use second-level headings for major tasks and third-level headings for details. Margin builds navigation from those headings.

### Keep the first version small

Write the shortest complete route to the outcome. Add alternatives only where the reader needs to make a decision. Code, diagrams, and tabs can explain a difficult step, but every section should still make sense as text.

## Preview and save

Use **Split view** to compare the Markdown with the rendered page. In the content details, keep the table of contents on the left, move it to the top or right, or switch it off.

Select **Save draft**. Your work remains private. The browser's local recovery is useful while writing; saving creates a server revision you can return to later.

## Choose a guide design

Open **Publication designer → Guides**. Try **Handbook** for a clear procedural layout, or **Publication suite** for coordinated articles and guides.

A combined template advertises its supported types. Applying it in Guides changes the guide design. Apply its Article configuration separately if you want the matching article layout.

Select **Save design** after reviewing your changes. Guide design settings apply to guides across this publication.

## Publish and check

Return to the draft and choose **Publish guide**. Open the public link and select an entry in **On this page** to jump to its heading.

On a narrow screen, side navigation moves above the body. The **Save** menu offers Markdown download and the browser's print-to-PDF view.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No table of contents | Add Markdown headings and enable contents in the page details. |
| A template is absent | Check that it supports Guide; article-only templates stay in Articles. |
| Your edits are not saved | Select Save draft or Save changes and check the status message. |
| Your guide has no chapters | This release uses standalone pages with heading navigation. |
